page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 belongs to the General Purpose Tau T2A family, featuring an Arm-based architecture. It is equipped with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs from an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a fixed 3.0 GHz clock speed with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache structures include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates hardware AES acceleration, while x86 vector extensions such as AVX and AMX are absent. This configuration features no bundled local storage and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the entry-level two-core profile. The server achieves mid-tier single-threaded throughput in stress-ng (1812.29) and single-threaded gzip compression (24.01 GB/sec). Multi-core processing is limited by the physical core count, as evidenced by Geekbench multi-core scores (1997.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (1596.29). Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 26.99 GB/sec, and write bandwidth measures 16.42 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 2.66 GB/sec, while in-memory operations achieve 2.61 million Redis SET operations per second.

The absence of local disks requires network-attached persistent storage for stateful services. Architectural cost efficiency is driven by the power-efficient Ampere Arm design, which provides consistent per-core execution without hyperthreading resource contention. Based on its resource sizing and benchmark results, the instance is suited for lightweight microservices, low-traffic web serving, ARMv8 development environments, and background containerized workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose, Arm-based virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Driven by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, each vCPU maps directly to a physical core with no hyperthreading contention. The platform features 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and hardware AES acceleration, but lacks x86 vector instructions. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, it provides moderate single-threaded compute and gzip compression, while multi-core benchmarks and memory bandwidth reflect its entry-level dual-core capacity. Memory bandwidth achieves 26.99 GB/sec for uncached reads, and in-memory key-value processing reaches 2.61 million Redis SET operations per second. The server is well matched for lightweight microservices, development pipelines, basic web serving, and containerized ARMv8 workloads requiring predictable single-thread execution.
